newsitem.title: UK: Most Britons wants to keep currency option open - poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Britons wants to keep currency option open - poll.

text.p: Most Britons want to keep open the option of joining a single European currency and an overwhelming majority want more information about the issue, according to an opinion poll published on Monday.
The poll for the European Movement showed that only 30 percent of people want the government to rule out joining the single currency now, while 60 percent favour keeping the option open.
Prime Minister John Major has repeatedly declined requests by so-called "Eurosceptics" to pledge never to join the European single currency and says Britain will keep its options open.

Of those questioned, 81 percent thought the government should publish detailed information setting out the advantages and disadvantages of the European single currency before deciding whether to join.

The survey also highlighted the extent of ignorance about European affairs in Britain with only 14 percent of those questioned describing their knowledge as good or very good. Some 49 percent described their EU knowledge as poor or very poor.
The poll, conducted by MORI, questioned 959 people.
